title: Generating running routes with GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work
raw_text: Here's a neat thing I had ChatGPT Work with GPT-6 Astra (Max) do this morning: I live at <my address>. Figure out 5K and 10K running routes from me that loop from my house. Use OSM data. It worked for 27 minutes and produced exactly what I'd asked for, as both an embedded visualization and downloadable GPX file and GeoJSON files. Here's that 5K route: When I asked it how it had created the route, it replied: I used Nominatim to locate the address and Overpass to download local OpenStreetMap roads and trails , then calculated the loops locally. Frustratingly, the actual code it ran and exact details of what it did weren't visible to me in the ChatGPT UI. I see this lack of transparency is an anti-feature. By the time I thought to ask for a copy of the Python code it had used, ChatGPT was unable to provide it. This appears to be because the thread had been compacted. I think any LLM system that uses compaction needs to both preserve the pre-compacted text and make that text available via agent tool calls, to protect against this kind of problem. As for displaying the map to me, that used the visualize skill . It created a file called /workspace/el-granada-5k-share.html to embed directly into the ChatGPT UI. Here's a copy of that HTML , which starts like this: < div id =" eg-share-loop " > < div class =" viz-row " > < h3 > El Granada harbor loop </ h3 > < span class =" text-small " > 5.1 km </ span > </ div > < div id =" eg-share-stage " > </ div > < div class =" text-small text

title: OpenAI agents attacked RubyGems back in May
raw_text: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed attack on RubyGems is a new bombshell report from Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen, and Sydney Von Arx - three of the four authors of the report on the agent attack on disused wikis ( previously ) last week. This time they're noting that it looks very likely that an OpenAI agent swarm was behind an attack against the RubyGems package repository first reported on May 12th by Maciej Mensfeld of the RubyGems security team : We're dealing with a major malicious attack on @rubygems right now. Signups are paused for the time being. Hundreds of packages involved - mostly targeting us, but some carrying exploits. The team has been on this for hours. More details to follow once we're through it. Those packages turned out to carry some very suspicious patterns: Many of them included "oai" in their name, or the author field, or the fake email address they provided. The files they were accessing were similar in character to the files retrieved by the wiki agents, using similar tricks (r.jina.ai) - and OpenAI have confirmed the wiki agents were theirs. The code in the packages appeared to be LLM-authored. I find point 2 the most convincing, given what we learned from the wiki attack when it was analyzed in September. title: So you want to use OpenRouter?
raw_text: So you want to use OpenRouter? One of OpenRouter's selling points is that it "handles fallbacks automatically and picks the most cost-effective option for each request", so you can call a single API endpoint for a model and get routed to the best available backend provider. Mohamed Moustafa points out a whole set of ways that this can cause you problems. Different providers run different serving software with different optimizations and settings, which means that the same OpenRouter endpoint can serve model requests that behave in different ways. Some providers even lack vision capability for vision models, and the way the reasoning effort option is processed can differ as well. Thankfully you can control which provider is routed to using the provider.only option . The /endpoints method returns the list of available providers for a specific model ID. title: Feeling sad about AI
raw_text: My comment on Feeling sad about AI — Hacker News. I'm not sure how useful it is to say this, but I think a lot of people (myself included, a few years ago now) have been through this moment of existential crisis and come out the other side. The initial reaction, when some coding agent does a piece of work that would have taken you a week in an hour and does it well , is to be very disheartened by it. Once you come to terms with the idea that translating an exact specification into decent code isn't a unique skill any more, you can start looking at the larger set of problems that you face as a software engineer and realize that there is so much left , and your existing skill and experience mean you can master these new tools, provide value, and execute at a level far greater than anyone who is just getting started building software using agents without any of your depth. If you don't want your profession to change at all then you're going to have a tough time with this - but that's surely been true for the history of software engineering? Has there ever been any stability to the tools and language we use beyond about a five year time horizon? These changes are happening a bit faster, but if you chose software development as a passion you've opted into pretty frequent radical change from the start. title: Soft-deprecating re.match()
raw_text: Soft-deprecating re.match() Python has a concept of soft deprecation , where APIs are marked as "should no longer be used to write new code" without any promise/threat to remove them in the future. Python 3.15 release manager Hugo van Kemenade describes how in the upcoming 3.15 release soft deprecation has come for the venerable but deeply confusing re.match() function. It's now available with the much clearer alternative re.prefixmatch() name - reflecting how it anchors at the beginning of the string but not the end. Most of the time you probably want re.search() (match this pattern anywhere in the string) or re.fullmatch() (match the entire string) instead. Via Lobste.rs Tags: python , regular-expressions

title: Don't sleep on wrapture
raw_text: Graham Dumpleton's new monkey patching package wrapture is shaping up to be an indispensable tool for Python developers. I'm not sure why I've seen so little buzz about it! Unit testing with wrapture - how to use it for the same kinds of thing as unittest.mock . Recording calls with wrapture - recording method calls as timelines and processing and displaying them as trees. Phased behaviour in wrapture - arranging patched methods to change behavior across multiple calls. Beyond callables in wrapture - monkey patching attributes, dictionaries, generators. Live tracing with wrapture - tracing a live application to see exactly how it works. title: Evolving Trends: A Bibliometric Analysis of Academic Librarians’ Publications at Twelve AAU Member Universities (New C&RL Journal Article)
raw_text: The article linked below was recently published by College & Research Libraries (C&RL) Title Evolving Trends : A Bibliometric Analysis of Academic Librarians’ Publications at Twelve AAU Member Universities Authors Pete E. Pascuzzi Purdue University Libraries Jason B. Reed Purdue University Libraries Greenley Goedde Creech Purdue University Libraries Source College & Research Libraries Vol 87, No 5 (2026) Vol 87, No 5 (2026) Abstract The goal of this bibliometric study was to explore the broader publication patterns of academic librarians in both information and library science (ISLS) and interdisciplinary research for the years 2009 to 2023. Web of Science data were collected for 12 academic libraries. The results showed that while the number of ISLS publications has dropped, interdisciplinary publications have increased dramatically with a broad range of disciplines represented, and that collaborations in the medical sciences were a major contributor to this increase. The study suggests that some academic libraries have shifted their priorities over the past 15 years and that the assessment of libraries’ scholarly publications must evolve to capture this shift. title: Disclosing AI Use in Academic Research, a New Global Study From Oxford University Press
raw_text: Published today by Oxford University Press (OUP): We have updated our author and editor guidelines on the responsible, appropriate, and transparent use of AI, including a policy outlining what AI use should be disclosed when preparing manuscripts for our journals. In a recent global survey of more than 2,600 researchers, nearly three-quarters (74%) of respondents revealed they were unclear what AI use they should disclose, despite there being strong support for disclosure. With 44% of researchers concerned that disclosing their use of AI will negatively impact how others view their work, and only 36% recording their AI use during their research, our survey emphasizes the growing gap between AI use and disclosure in academic research, and recognizes the need for clear disclosure policies. Direct to Full Text Report (59 pages; PDF) Selected Findings From the Survey: 64% of researchers report AI as beneficial to their research, with over two-thirds (68%) using AI chatbots on the open web for their research, and just under half (49%) using machine translation. AI tools are most commonly used for discovering existing research (55%), summarizing existing research (46%), and editing the write-up of research (45%). Many (68%) agree that AI tools can reduce accessibility barriers, too. However, 35% of those in the arts and humanities never use AI tools in their research, as opposed to 15% and 18% for STM and the social sciences, respectively. title: Vacature: Metadataspecialist digitale preservering bij de KB nationale bibliotheek
raw_text: Als metadataspecialist digitale preservering werk je aan de toekomst van de nationale digitale collectie. Jij zorgt dat wat vandaag wordt gearchiveerd, ook over tientallen jaren nog vindbaar en begrijpelijk is. Wat ga je doen? De KB beheert miljoenen digitale objecten, zoals webarchieven, gedigitaliseerde boeken en tijdschriften en born-digital publicaties. Om deze collecties ook op de lange termijn vindbaar en begrijpelijk te houden, is betrouwbare metadata essentieel. Daar draag jij als metadataspecialist direct aan bij. Je werkt met een gespecialiseerd preserveringssysteem waarin metadata wordt vastgelegd over onder andere de herkomst, geschiedenis en technische eigenschappen van bestanden. Je specificeert, implementeert, test en documenteert deze metadata en stelt de specificaties op voor transformaties tussen verschillende (meta)dataformaten. Dit werk wordt ondersteund met specialistische tooling. Daarbij werk je nauw samen met collega’s zoals contentanalisten, informatiespecialisten en digital preservation officers. Ook deel je actief kennis binnen en buiten de KB, bijvoorbeeld via presentaties of deelname aan gebruikersgroepen en congressen. title: Directeur van door Trump tegengewerkte Smithsonian-instituut vertrekt
raw_text: Directeur Lonnie Bunch van het Amerikaanse Smithsonian-instituut stapt na zeven jaar op. Het instituut staat onder druk sinds het aantreden van president Donald Trump. De manier waarop Smithsonian de Amerikaanse geschiedenis en samenleving presenteert staat haaks op het MAGA-gedachtegoed. Trump heeft daarom de aanval geopend op het Smithsonian, dat tientallen nationale musea, bibliotheken en onderwijs- en onderzoeksinstituten omvat. Tentoonstellingen en collecties moeten worden geschrapt en de regering dreigde recent subsidie aan het Smithsonian helemaal stop te zetten. Het instituut bestaat al sinds de 19de eeuw en functioneert onafhankelijk van de regering. Vrijwillig vertrek Tegen The New Yor k Times heeft Bunch, de eerste zwarte Amerikaan aan het hoofd van het Smithsonian, gezegd dat kritiek vanuit het Witte Huis geen aanleiding is geweest voor zijn vertrek. ‘Het was simpelweg gewoon tijd’, aldus Bunch, die nu 73 jaar is. Hij geeft wel aan dat de baan erg stressvol is geweest de laatste jaren. Eerder was Bunch verantwoordelijk voor de opening van het Nationaal Museum voor Afro-Amerikaanse Geschiedenis en Cultuur aan de National Mall in Washington D.C.. Het museum is onderdeel van het Smithsonian en wordt regelmatig onder vuur genomen door de MAGA-beweging. Het museum zou te veel nadruk leggen op het slavernijverleden van de Verenigde Staten. title: Taalhuis Veenendaal bestaat 10 jaar
raw_text: Het Taalhuis van Bibliotheek Veenendaal bestaat dit jaar tien jaar. Al die jaren zetten medewerkers en vrijwilligers zich in om inwoners te helpen bij basisvaardigheden, zoals de het spreken en begrijpen van de Nederlandse taal, omgaan met cijfers en digitale vaardigheden. Geraldine Floor (71) is vrijwilliger van het eerste uur. Als taalbegeleider ontmoet zij wekelijks iemand die Nederlands wil leren. ‘Het is mooi om te zien hoe mensen de taal oppakken.’ Geraldine hoeft niet lang na te denken over wat haar vrijwilligerswerk zo leuk maakt. ‘Je leert mensen uit andere landen kennen. En je leert zelf ook hoe onze taal in elkaar zit. Ik heb geen onderwijsachtergrond, maar ontdekte al snel dat nadruk op uitspraak heel belangrijk is. Het juist schrijven volgt dan vaak vanzelf.’ In de afgelopen tien jaar begeleidde Geraldine mensen met verschillende achtergronden. Zo hielp ze mensen uit Syrië, Afghanistan en Servië, maar ook een Koerdische tandarts. Op dit moment begeleidt ze een Engelse. ‘Voor haar is het lastig om Nederlands te oefenen. title: Now Available: Clarivate Releases Pulse of the Library 2026 Survey Report
raw_text: From Clarivate : Clarivate today released the Pulse of the Library 2026 report. Now in its third year, the global survey examines how libraries are responding to technological change, including AI, shifting priorities and growing demands on staff and resources. The findings reveal that Mainland China recorded the highest level of AI implementation, with 28% reporting moderate to active implementation, more than double the rate in 2024 and well above the 16% global figure. The report also shows a widening gap between libraries moving beyond experimentation with AI and those still in the earliest stages of AI adoption. 51% of libraries in active implementation operate under joint library and IT governance, against 26% of the sample overall, signaling the importance of structured governance models and interdepartmental collaboration. Oren Beit-Arie, Senior Vice President, Strategy & Innovation, Academia & Government at Clarivate, said: “For libraries, AI marks a continuous shift along with a set of hard choices about when to adopt, when to hold back and how to protect academic integrity and library core values. What stands out in this year’s research are the differences between libraries choosing to experiment, learn and build confidence with AI and those taking a wait-and-see approach, whether by choice or because resources are limited.” Other key findings from the report include: Concerns are evolving as implementation advances. title: Building Leadership Through Associations: A Conversation with Loida Garcia-Febo
raw_text: How can library associations strengthen leadership and help library and information professionals respond to increasingly complex and uncertain environments? On 25 June 2026, Loida Garcia-Febo, Chair of the IFLA Management of Library Associations Section (MLAS) , joined a conversation with Roxana Huaman Huriarte, Chair of the IFLA Latin America and the Caribbean Regional Division , and Nick Boxem, Chair of the IFLA Europe Regional Division , both members of the IFLA Regional Council leadership group. The conversation explored leadership within IFLA and library associations, and how strategic planning, capacity building and professional networks can help organisations and individuals respond more effectively to change. Leadership is a capacity that can be developed Leadership is not simply linked to holding a formal position but it is a capacity that can be intentionally developed through experience, training, mentoring, coaching and opportunities to work with others. For library associations, this means creating environments where current and emerging leaders can learn, test ideas, build confidence and develop the skills required to guide organisations through change. Garcia-Febo highlighted the importance of leadership training, mentoring and coaching, alongside team building and effective communication. title: Samenwerking bibliotheek Gelderland Zuid (Nijmegen) met eigenaren minibiebs
raw_text: Nijmegen telt honderden minibiebs, de kleine boekenkastjes die je in de straat vindt. Wouter van Balveren, innovatiemanager bij OBGZ (Nijmegen en omstreken) vertelt aan Probiblio.nl dat de bieb de kleine boekenkastjes niet als bedreiging ziet, maar juist als stimulans. ‘De eigenaren zijn enthousiaste mensen die van lezen houden en het leuk vinden om boeken en verhalen met anderen te delen. Die staan gewoon in woonwijken, soms bijna in iedere straat.’ De Nijmeegse bibliotheek ondersteunt de minibiebs op verschillende manieren. ‘We kijken naar waar wij als openbare bibliotheek iets kunnen toevoegen. title: New Freckle Project Report Examines 15 Years of Public Library Use
raw_text: From EveryLibrary Institute: A new Freckle Project Report, “15 Years of IMLS Figures” , looks at national public library statistics from 2010 through 2024 and identifies a striking contrast: American public libraries have more facilities, more staff, and higher levels of funding than at any point in the period examined, while several major measures of physical library use remain substantially below their 2010 levels. The Freckle Project is led by researcher Tim Coates, and its publication is supported by the EveryLibrary Institute. The August 2026 Report examines 15 years of data from the Institute of Museum and Library Services on America’s public libraries. In 2024, the United States had 17,580 public library facilities and 147,289 library employees, while public libraries received nearly $18 billion for operations and another $1.6 billion for capital expenditures. Yet annual visits declined from approximately 1.57 billion in 2010 to 869 million in 2024, while total circulation fell from approximately 2.47 billion to 1.71 billion. Coates’s analysis highlights an especially significant decline in adult physical circulation. After subtracting electronic and children’s circulation from total circulation, he estimates that this category fell approximately 68 percent between 2010 and 2024. title: Bibliothecaris VS die zich verzette tegen LHBTQ+-censuur ontvangt schikking na ontslag
raw_text: Saline County in het Amerikaanse Arkansas moet 275.000 dollar betalen in een zaak tegen een bibliotheekdirecteur die zich verzette tegen censuur van LHBTQ+-boeken op de kinderafdeling. Ze werd daarop ontslagen. Een burgerrechtenorganisatie spande een rechtszaak aan en het kwam tot een schikking. Burgerrechtenorganisatie ACLU van Arkansas greep in toen directeur Patty Hector in 2023 was ontslagen vanwege haar kritiek op een verordening die voorschreef dat boeken met ‘seksuele inhoud of afbeeldingen’ uit de kinderafdeling moesten worden verwijderd. ‘Zwijgen nooit de oplossing’ ‘Het opkomen voor de vrijheid om te lezen heeft me mijn baan gekost, en de carrière waar ik zo van hield, maar ik heb nooit geloofd dat zwijgen de oplossing was’, zegt Hector tegen Advocate .com . ‘Bibliotheken zijn van iedereen. Bibliothecarissen moeten hun gemeenschap volgens professionele normen van dienst kunnen zijn, zonder bang te hoeven zijn voor politieke represailles. Ik hoop dat deze schikking een signaal afgeeft aan bibliothecarissen en andere ambtenaren in heel Arkansas dat hun stem en hun grondwettelijke rechten ertoe doen.’ Hectors ontslag viel samen met een Amerikaanse conservatieve campagne om de toegang tot boeken te beperken, waaronder veel titels met LHBTQ+-thema’s. Hector stelde destijds dat deze boeken niet als ongeschikt voor kinderen mogen worden beschouwd. ‘Het is niet illegaal om homo of trans te zijn’, zei ze tijdens een openbare hoorzitting. title: IFLA Europe Regional Division Webinar 2026: How EURDC supports Libraries across Europe
raw_text: The IFLA Europe Regional Division invites library professionals, information specialists, and IFLA members from across Europe to an engaging online webinar on 1 October 2026 at 11:00 CEST . Over the past five years, the Europe Regional Division Committee (EURDC) has worked to strengthen collaboration, advocacy, and engagement among libraries and library professionals throughout Europe. Despite these efforts, many colleagues remain unfamiliar with the division’s mandate, activities, and opportunities for involvement. This webinar aims to change that. During the session, four members of the current EURDC Committee, representing Finland, Germany, Norway, and Portugal, will introduce the division’s work and share practical examples of how EURDC supports the European library community. Participants will gain insights into the division’s objectives, ongoing initiatives, and future priorities. The webinar will also provide an opportunity for dialogue. Attendees will be encouraged to share their expectations, discuss challenges facing libraries in Europe, and suggest ways in which EURDC can better support their work and professional communities. The event will be conducted in English via Zoom, with automated subtitles available to improve accessibility. title: The Management of Library Associations Section (MLAS) WLIC 2026 Outcomes Report
raw_text: Part of MLAS Members and Attendees at MLAS Business Meeting in Busan The IFLA Management of Library Associations Section (MLAS) had an active and substantive presence at the IFLA World Library and Information Congress (WLIC) 2026 in Busan. Activities included the MLAS Business Meeting, MLAS Open Session, IFLA Associations Meeting, an informal meeting of International Relations Chairs, and opportunities for congress attendees to connect with the MLAS Chair at the IFLA exhibition booth. Across these activities, common priorities emerged: strategic renewal, member engagement, leadership, partnerships, advocacy, financial sustainability, visibility, digital transformation and AI, resilience, crisis preparedness, and responsiveness to changing societal needs. These priorities are closely aligned with MLAS’s mission to support strong, well-managed library associations through leadership, peer learning, resource development, and effective association practices worldwide. Strong library associations do not simply have strategies. They make their strategies visible, translate them into action, engage their members, build partnerships, advocate effectively, develop new leaders, sustain their organisations, and continually renew themselves in response to change. In het 12-jarige bestaan van Hebban is dit de eerste keer dat één boek meerdere Hebban prijzen in de wacht sleept. De Hebban Debuutprijs geeft Nederlandstalige debutanten een extra podium en is de enige literaire juryprijs van Nederland en Vlaanderen met een grote invloed van lezers. De winnaar ontvangt een award, een cheque van € 1.500 en een campagne ter waarde van € 2.500 op Hebban.nl, in de Hebban App, de nieuwsbrieven en op de socialemediakanalen van Hebban. Uit juryrapport: ‘Hier komen originaliteit, taalkunst, zintuiglijkheid en maatschappelijke urgentie samen in een boek dat de Nederlandstalige literatuur nog miste.
